### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s).

**38** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 256a4b725116859f891160ad71b21c2e092d1fb0`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 256a4b725116859f891160ad71b21c2e092d1fb0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0aa98ca78948af94ead17e73c136b10142c939b2` — the merge of head `dc804fbb17e230449f01be794255263eea9ffd06` into base `256a4b725116859f891160ad71b21c2e092d1fb0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0aa98ca78948af94ead17e73c136b10142c939b2 && git checkout 0aa98ca78948af94ead17e73c136b10142c939b2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 256a4b725116859f891160ad71b21c2e092d1fb0 dc804fbb17e230449f01be794255263eea9ffd06 && git checkout -B drift-repro 256a4b725116859f891160ad71b21c2e092d1fb0 && git merge --no-ff dc804fbb17e230449f01be794255263eea9ffd06

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 256a4b725116859f891160ad71b21c2e092d1fb0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 256a4b725116859f891160ad71b21c2e092d1fb0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Contract review for card #30621 · narrowing face (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`) · read-only reviewer at the contract-review tier, brief per `record-recognisers --brief-template --face narrowing` · 2026-11-06T14:37Z

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6a24dc2567408d3726317e55a2454d1f31c030d2`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/rule-criteria.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/rule-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-object-enforcement.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/federated-phantom-anchors.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/declared-sharing-rules.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/index.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-hook-dispatch.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-execution-plumbing.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/rest/src/sharing-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/error-response.ts, packages/rest/src/batch-routes.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-sharing-rule-enforceability.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, docs/adr/0111-record-share-management-authority-and-verb-boundary.md, content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx (read as the published spec), hotcrm `src/sales/sharing/demo-staffing.ts` and its `crm_*` objects (read as the consumer)

Inputs: card #30621 (body, triage 6685173622, claim 6685311068 and its re-post 6685434298, os-dev-report 6686849997), PR #30953 (body, file list, net diff against `main` at the head), the head's check-runs. The review tree is `main` at 4d56914a (2026-11-06), on which the head's six code files differ from `main` by exactly the PR's hunks.

Check-runs on the head (read 2026-11-06, every run concluded): 38 `success`, 12 `skipped` (the UI lanes, the opt-in harnesses and the schedule gate, none of which the diff reaches), 0 `failure`. The ten required contexts that this PR's paths engage all concluded `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (8 of 8 shards), `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Live E2E UI`, `Test UI`; `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI` and `Build & E2E UI` were `skipped` by the path filter. Also green: `Check Changeset`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Spec property liveness`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`. These conclusions are the gate verdicts this record adopts.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged against the cited code:

1. **`/data` insert on `sys_sharing_rule` (non-system caller)** — refused with `SHARING_NOT_ENABLED` / 422 when `SharingService.objectInertReason(object_name)` is non-null; saved otherwise. **Right.** The engine dispatches `beforeInsert` once per row for an array insert too (`engine.ts` `rowHookContexts`, `dispatch.mode: 'per-row'`), so a batch insert is checked row by row; the guard's `Array.isArray(data)` early return is unreachable on the engine's own path (observation, harmless).
2. **`/data` update on `sys_sharing_rule` (non-system caller)** — checked only when `object_name` is supplied and differs from `ctx.previous.object_name`; a patch that keeps the object (switch-off, relabel, criteria edit) passes. **Right, and fail-closed on the shapes the brief asked about:** the by-id path binds `previous` from the pre-image, the predicate path dispatches per matched row with `previous` bound (`dispatchPerRowBeforeHooks`), and a dispatch that carries no `previous` falls through to the check rather than past it. A move plus a rename in one patch is judged on the object alone, which is the only field this guard owns; the declared-name guard beside it judges the rename.
3. **`SharingRuleService.defineRule` (non-system caller)** — refused when no row of that name is stored in the caller's organization, or the stored row sits on a different object; an upsert that keeps the stored object is not a move. **Right.** The `existing` read is `{ name, organization_id: orgId }` under the system context for every organization-scoped caller, so "stored on the same object" cannot be spoofed with another organization's row. The organization-less platform operator keeps the pre-existing `{ name }` lookup; that is `main`'s upsert behaviour, not widened or narrowed here.
4. **`assertNotInertGrant` refactor** — now `objectInertReason` plus the throw; the verdict and the message are byte-identical to `main`'s. **Right.** The grant pre-flight (`grant()`, both the system and the non-system arm) and `assertSharingEnforced` are unchanged in effect.
5. **The refusal envelope** — `SharingRuleObjectNotEnforcedError` carries `code: 'SHARING_NOT_ENABLED'`, `status: 422`, the same declared pair `DeclaredSharingRuleNameConflictError` (409) carries on the same two doors; `classifiedRefusalAnswer` reads `declaredHttpStatus` plus `code`, and the sharing-rule route's `handleError` relays it. `SHARING_NOT_ENABLED` is in the `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` row of `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` (`error-code-ledger.zod.ts:667`); no `packages/spec` change, none needed. **Right.**
6. **Public surface** — `index.ts` is untouched, so `SharingRuleObjectNotEnforcedError`, `bindRuleObjectEnforcementGuard` and `RULE_OBJECT_ENFORCEMENT_GUARD_PACKAGE` are not package exports; `SharingService` is exported, so `sharingRuleObjectRefusal` is a new public method on an exported class (additive). `ISharingService` / `ISharingRuleService` in the spec are unchanged. **Right** for a `patch` with a BREAKING banner (the break is the accept set, not the surface).
7. **System writes pass** — `buildSession` propagates `isSystem` onto `ctx.session`, so the platform's own writers (upgrade-harness fixtures, migrations, the ownership ceremony, `defineRule`'s own system write) are untouched, mirroring `bindDeclaredRuleNameGuard`. **Right.**
8. **Binding and rebinding** — bound inside `kernel:ready` in the `enforce !== false` branch after `this.service` is constructed unconditionally, so the `if (this.service)` cannot skip it; it carries its own `packageId`, so `unbindAllRuleHooks` on every rule rebind leaves it standing. An `enforce: false` host binds no guard, exactly as it binds no criteria guard and evaluates no rule. **Right.**
9. **The consumer** — hotcrm installs nine stored rules (`demo-staffing.ts`) on `crm_opportunity`, `crm_lead`, `crm_task`, `crm_event`, `crm_case`, each declared `sharingModel: 'private'` with an `owner_id` column: all admitted. **Unaffected.**

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/30621-sharing-rule-object-not-enforced.md`: `'@objectstack/plugin-sharing': patch`, the BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` (a listed category). The PR body carries the same two declaration lines and the title is `fix(plugin-sharing)!:`. **Matches what the diff publishes:** the only released package the diff moves is `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`; a save-door narrowing with no key added, removed, renamed or re-shaped is a non-protocol narrowing, which ships `patch` with its banner and disposition; declared `sharingRules` (the authorable metadata) are read from the registry (ADR-0131 D2) and never meet either door, so `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. Stored rows are neither migrated nor deleted, so there is no migration to prescribe. `Check Changeset` and `Lint · docs & code guards` concluded `success` on the head.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — adopted.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []` — nothing to answer.
- `security_findings: none` — agreed; the refusal removes only rows no gate would ever consult (ADR-0111 D7), and a system write still passes.
- `premise_still_valid: true` — agreed: the card's expected behaviour (refuse at save, name the object, say how to enable sharing) is what the tree does.
- `out_of_scope_findings` 1 (lint `anchorFindings` reports a declared rule on a public-model object as inert while the runtime admits its external recipients, #25549): a real divergence in the fail-closed direction, in `packages/lint`, outside this card's surface; **escalated to the lane as a card to file**, nothing owed by this PR.
- `out_of_scope_findings` 2 (#30209 row 5, the object picker): carried by #30209; this PR is that card's option C on the save side, as the card itself says.
- Claim fences: no path under `packages/spec/**` or `ui/**` in the file list; held.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing against the published spec on `main`.** ADR-0111 D7 ("grants that would enforce nothing are refused at write time rather than persisted as inert rows"), its 2026-10-24 amendment for #25549 (a public object whose `owner_id` is real admits an `external` recipient; every other recipient keeps the 422; `controlled_by_parent` stays refused), ADR-0078 (no silently inert metadata) and ADR-0049 all declare the refusal; `validate-sharing-rule-enforceability` already makes it real for a DECLARED rule's anchor at authoring (`anchorFindings`). The stored-rule save doors were the one authoring surface where the refusal was not real: the row saved and the reconcile refused every grant. The PR makes the spec's own refusal real at the rule's door. It takes no declared capability away: the only rules it refuses are those whose every grant the reconcile refuses on `main` today, and the recipient-decided arm (public model, real owner column) stays admitted exactly as the amendment and the sharing-rules page's external-recipients paragraph declare it. Not an implementation gap narrowed at the consumer; the spec's refusal, delivered.

**Probes:**

- *Can a non-system caller reach a non-enforced object another way?* Batch insert: per-row `beforeInsert` dispatch, checked. Predicate update: per-row `beforeUpdate` with `previous` bound, checked when it moves the object. A missing pre-image: falls to the check, refused. Rename plus move in one patch: the object compare does not depend on the name. The generic batch route (`batch-routes.ts`) writes through `ql.insert` / `ql.update`, so the hooks fire; the engine has no `upsert` verb and the REST layer exposes none. The one remaining door is a system-context write, left open by design (the platform's own writers) and harmless: the reconcile still refuses every grant such a row asks for.
- *Is `defineRule`'s `existing` lookup by name within the right organization?* Yes for every organization-scoped caller (`{ name, organization_id: orgId }`, read under the system context). The organization-less platform operator's `{ name }` lookup is `main`'s behaviour and is not touched (observation, not a finding of this PR).
- *Does the save verdict equal what the reconcile refuses?* The reconcile materialises through `this.sharing.grant(...)` under the system context (`sharing-rule-service.ts:2399`), whose pre-flight is `assertNotInertGrant` over `objectInertReason` and then `assertRecipientNotInert` per recipient. The save door refuses iff `objectInertReason` is non-null, i.e. iff the reconcile refuses every grant on the object whoever the recipient is. The recipient-decided arm (#25549) is admitted at save and refused per internal recipient at reconcile, which is the declared behaviour. Federated objects: a non-public object whose `owner_id` is the injected phantom anchor is refused on both (the `hasPhantomOwnerAnchor` arm); a public one with the anchor is refused on both (the generic arm, since the external lift requires a real column); one whose author declared a real remote `owner_id` is admitted on both. An object the engine has no schema for is admitted on both. Equal.
- *Can boot-time seeding or package install now fail or abort boot?* No. Declared `sharingRules` are read from the registry on every read of the rule set (ADR-0131 D2, `declared-sharing-rules.ts`) and are never written to `sys_sharing_rule`; `defineRule`'s only in-tree caller is the REST route with the request's own context; upgrade-harness fixtures and the stored-row migrations write under the system context, which the guard lets pass; the guard throws only inside a non-system write, and nothing at boot is one. The hotcrm installer's rules all sit on private, owned objects.

**Findings:**

- **should-fix** — `sharingRuleObjectRemedy` names the wrong remedy for a PUBLIC federated object whose `owner_id` is the injected phantom anchor. `objectInertReason` refuses it through the generic "public sharing model or no owner_id" arm (the external lift requires a real column), and the remedy then falls to the last sentence, "give the object a private or read-only sharing model and an `owner_id` field". The object already has an `owner_id`, and following the sentence (declare `private`) lands the author on the phantom-anchor refusal. Test `hasPhantomOwnerAnchor(schema)` before the model, so a federated object is told to declare a real remote `owner_id` whatever its model. Message only; the verdict is right, and the four refusal pins hold either way.
- **observation (prose, outside this review's floor)** — the paragraph the PR adds to `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx` sits directly under `main`'s sentence "On a `public_read_write` object, or a system object with no `sharingModel`, a share or sharing rule takes effect for external recipients only"; for an owner-less system object the two now read against each other, and the ADR's wording ("whose `owner_id` is real") is the precise one. For the lane's next docs touch.
- **observation** — the `Array.isArray(data)` early return in `bindRuleObjectEnforcementGuard` is dead on the engine's per-row dispatch; harmless, and shared with the criteria guard.

No must-fix.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-lpcxlh`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4czvZykUqhYxYXSSDt4`

**VERDICT: PASS**

Delta contract review for card #30621 · PR #30953 · narrowing face (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`) · read-only reviewer at the contract-review tier · delta 6a24dc25..dc804fbb17e230449f01be794255263eea9ffd06 on top of the PASS record for 6a24dc2567408d3726317e55a2454d1f31c030d2 (comment 6687390627) · 2026-11-06

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dc804fbb17e230449f01be794255263eea9ffd06`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-object-enforcement.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts + content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx (read as the published spec), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/federated-phantom-anchors.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/rule-hooks.ts (unchanged, read for the door), docs/adr/0111-record-share-management-authority-and-verb-boundary.md (D7 and its 2026-10-24 amendment)

This is a delta review: it re-judges the one commit pushed since the prior PASS record (dc804fbb, "name the federated-anchor remedy before the model, and reconcile the sharing-rules page with D7's real owner_id"), read through `gh api` compare and the contents API at the head; the prior record's judgments ①1–9 stand for everything the delta does not touch. The compare is `ahead 1, behind 0` and touches exactly three files: `sharing-service.ts` (+4/−1, one hunk), `sharing-rule-object-enforcement.test.ts` (+26/−1), `sharing-rules.mdx` (+9/−8).

Check-runs on the head (read 2026-11-06, every run concluded after the `Test Core` aggregate finished): 50 runs, 38 `success`, 12 `skipped` (the UI lanes, the opt-in harnesses and the schedule gate, none of which the delta reaches), 0 `failure`. The required contexts this PR's paths engage all concluded `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (8 of 8 shards and the aggregate), `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Live E2E UI`, `Test UI`; `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI` and `Build & E2E UI` were `skipped` by the path filter. Also green: `Check Changeset`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Build Docs`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Spec property liveness`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`. These conclusions are the gate verdicts this record adopts.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The should-fix is closed in the tree.** `sharingRuleObjectRemedy` now tests the phantom-anchor arm before the model: the condition `schema && effectiveSharingModel(schema) !== 'public' && hasOwnerField(schema) && hasPhantomOwnerAnchor(schema)` became `schema && hasOwnerField(schema) && hasPhantomOwnerAnchor(schema)`. The remedy order is now bypass → `controlled_by_parent` → injected-anchor federated object (any model) → generic. A PUBLIC federated object whose `owner_id` is the registry's injected anchor is therefore told "declare a real remote `owner_id` column on the federated object" instead of "give the object a private or read-only sharing model and an `owner_id` field" — the sentence that led the author onto the phantom-anchor refusal. **Right.** The retained `hasOwnerField` guard is redundant with `hasPhantomOwnerAnchor` (the anchor is the injected field, so the provenance verdict implies presence) and harmless: where no `owner_id` is registered at all, the generic remedy is the correct one.
2. **The delta is message-only; no accept set moves.** The service hunk is the single remedy condition. `objectInertReason`, `inertGrantReason`, `recipientDecidesInertness`, `assertNotInertGrant`, the `sys_sharing_rule` hook guard (`rule-hooks.ts`) and `SharingRuleService.defineRule` are untouched by the delta, so `sharingRuleObjectRefusal` returns `null` exactly when it did at 6a24dc25 and the same objects are refused on both doors. Walked per arm: a public federated object with the injected anchor was refused before and after through `inertGrantReason`'s generic arm (the `#25549` lift requires `!hasPhantomOwnerAnchor(schema)`, so it never reaches `null`); its `reason` half is byte-identical and only the remedy half changes. A non-public phantom-anchor object: same sentence as before. A public object with a real `owner_id`: `null`, unchanged. An owner-less object: generic remedy, unchanged. A `controlled_by_parent` detail and a bypass object: earlier returns, unchanged. **Right.**
3. **The new pin.** `describe('[#30621] the refusal sentence names the remedy for the arm that refused')` registers `os30621_ext_customer` as `sharingModel: 'public_read_write'` with `external: { remoteName: 'customers' }` and no declared `owner_id`, first asserts the registry injected the anchor (`getSchema(...).fields.owner_id` truthy, so the test cannot pass vacuously on a schema that never reached the phantom arm), then asserts the refusal names the object, carries the remote-column remedy and not the generic `sharingModel: 'private'` one, and that the `/data` insert is refused `SHARING_NOT_ENABLED` / 422 with nothing stored. It pins both halves: the corrected remedy and the unchanged verdict. The object is registered and deliberately left out of `driver.initObjects` — correct, a federated object has no platform-provisioned storage and nothing in the pin writes to it. `boot()` additionally returns `sharing` (additive; the earlier call sites destructure by name). The pin went into the component's existing harness file as a top-level `describe`, as the shared-harness rule requires. **Right.**
4. **The prose now agrees with ADR-0111 D7.** The external-recipients paragraph gained the amendment's own qualifier, "whose `owner_id` is real", matching D7's "On an object whose effective model is `public` and whose `owner_id` is real (not a federated phantom anchor)". The refusal paragraph now enumerates exactly the arms D7.2 and its amendment refuse for every recipient: an object with no real `owner_id` (a system object without one such as `sys_session`, or a federated object whose `owner_id` is the platform's injected anchor), a `controlled_by_parent` detail, a bypass object — and no longer says "a public object with no owner", the phrase that read against the paragraph above it for an owner-less system object. A non-system `private` object with no `owner_id`, also refused by D7.2, falls under "an object with no real `owner_id`"; the parenthetical gives examples, not the full set, which is fine. `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Check Documentation Links` and `Build Docs` concluded `success` on the head. **Agrees.**
5. **Nothing new broken.** `index.ts` and the spec are untouched, so the public surface judged in the prior record (one additive method on the exported `SharingService`) is unchanged; no new export, no envelope change, no registry change. The consumer (hotcrm's nine stored rules on private, owned `crm_*` objects) is unaffected by a remedy sentence. **Unaffected.**

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from the prior record: `.changeset/30621-sharing-rule-object-not-enforced.md` (`'@objectstack/plugin-sharing': patch`, BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`) is not touched by the delta and needs no edit — a refusal-sentence wording, a test and a docs reconciliation publish nothing new. `Check Changeset` concluded `success` on the head.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — adopted.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []` — nothing new to answer.
- `security_findings: none` — agreed; the delta changes a prescription sentence and documentation, never a verdict.
- `premise_still_valid: true` — agreed.
- `out_of_scope_findings`: none new; the two carried by the prior record (lint `anchorFindings` on a public-model object, #25549 divergence; #30209 row 5) stand as recorded there.
- Claim fences: no path under `packages/spec/**`, `ui/**` or any governed-register row in the delta; `content/docs/**` is not a governed surface. Held.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing against the published spec on `main`, re-read for the delta.** The prior record's judgment holds: the PR makes D7's own refusal real at the sharing rule's save doors and takes no declared capability away. The delta sharpens the one place the prescription disagreed with the arm that refused — a federated object already has the field the generic sentence told its author to add, and the model it told them to declare lands on the phantom-anchor refusal — so the sentence an administrator is shown now names the only remedy that would admit the rule (a real remote `owner_id` column, or an `external.columnMap` entry for one, per `federated-phantom-anchors.ts`). The page's two paragraphs now read as D7's two halves: the recipient-decided arm on an effective-public object with a real `owner_id`, and the for-every-recipient refusals.

**Probes:**

- *Does the reordered remedy ever change which objects are refused?* No. `sharingRuleObjectRemedy` is reached only after `objectInertReason` returned a non-null reason, and that function is not in the delta.
- *Could the phantom arm now fire on a local object?* No. `hasPhantomOwnerAnchor` is `isOwnerAnchorUnprovable` from `@objectstack/spec/data`, provenance `injected-unprovisioned` plus the `columnMap` arm; a local object's injected `owner_id` is provisioned, and an inexact match answers `false`.
- *Does the test's federated registration survive the real engine?* The pin's first assertion checks the anchor was injected, and the suite ran green in `Test Core` on the head.
